items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: BUG path (no formal spec doc). Implements exactly the fix the operator specified: _apply_retention now also unlinks each victim's evidence_file_for(...) sibling, unchanged unless retention itself is reworked (out of scope, deferred separately). No extra features added.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: The new sibling unlink is wrapped in try/except (EvidenceError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) so a legacy-shaped run_id (RUN_ID_LEGACY-only, no evidence ever installed) or a raced-away sibling cannot crash retention -- matches the existing entry-file unlink's own failure tolerance.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input, no SQL/HTML, no secrets. Path is derived from validated run_id via the existing evidence_file_for resolver, which already defends against traversal/symlink escape.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Two new tests assert outcomes (file presence/absence), not internals: test_retention_sweeps_evidence_sibling_of_evicted_entries (happy path -- sibling actually removed) and test_apply_retention_survives_missing_evidence_sibling (no sibling ever existed -- must not raise). Both were run RED against the pre-fix code first (only the happy-path one failed, confirming the bug), then GREEN after the fix. Full retention/append/race/overshoot suite (36 tests) still green.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: One extra unlink() syscall per evicted entry (bounded by keep_last churn per append, typically 0-1). No new loops, no N+1 pattern.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: No new files. append_iterate_entry.py (436->451 lines) and its test file (509->546) were already over the 300-line grandfathered bloat-baseline cap before this change; both entries were refreshed in shipwright_bloat_baseline.json to their new measured line counts (via the tool's own _file_newlines(), not wc -l) so the anti-ratchet pre-commit gate reads them as intentional, not a silent ratchet. Re-verified anti_ratchet_check.py --staged is clean.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: No new serialized format or producer/consumer pair introduced. The change completes an existing deletion operation using the existing evidence_file_for(project_root, run_id) resolver -- the same path function install_current_evidence already writes through -- so there is no new boundary to round-trip probe. touches_io_boundary did not fire in classify_complexity.py's diff-driven detector.
